question: Do heuristic-usable tracks establish reliable product masks?
boundedTakeaway: All samples passed the worker heuristics; assistant inspection found apparent mask errors. Projection discrepancy is not visible-silhouette accuracy.

metric.unit: frame diagonal; multiplied by 100 for display
metric.aggregation: per-sequence arithmetic mean over heuristic-usable non-seed samples
metric.missingness: excluded sequences remain in CSV; no zero imputation

coverage.meaning: passes worker uncertainty heuristics, not an accuracy or usable-take judgment

privacy: Metadata only; no footage, frames, pixel annotations or signed URLs included.
limitations: Convenience sample from upstream test indices, not FlowBlock confirmation data
Projected 3D boxes are not visible silhouettes; metrics are discrepancy proxies, not mask accuracy
No creator treatment, usability judgment, calibrated confidence or camera-distance inference
Eight source videos are the evaluation units; 592 non-seed samples are temporally dependent, not 592 independent trials.
Usable means passing worker tracking heuristics, not creator-rated usable footage.
Projection discrepancy compares different label definitions and must not be called tracking accuracy.
Processing timing excludes model construction and includes no queue.
The native run imports recorded local MPS execution; no remote GPU allocation is implied.
Assistant visual inspection found apparent mask errors in three sampled views despite 100% heuristic-usable coverage. Qualitative observations are not independent ground-truth accuracy scores.
